subject: maths-aa-sl
author: original (NevaIB)
title: Three-dimensional geometry

points.text: Volume and surface area of pyramids, cones, spheres, hemispheres and combinations
Angle between two intersecting lines, and between a line and a plane

bigPicture: Coordinate geometry and solids extend to 3D. Most 3D angle problems reduce to finding a right-angled triangle inside the shape.

keyIdeas.answer: d = √(Δx² + Δy² + Δz²); midpoint = average each coordinate.
Pyramid, cone (volume and curved area), sphere (volume and surface) are in the booklet; a hemisphere is half a sphere plus a circle if the flat face counts.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you find the angle between a line and a plane?
keyIdeas.answer: Drop a perpendicular from the line to the plane, then use trig in the right-angled triangle formed with the line's projection.

keyTerms.def: shadow of a line on a plane
l in πrl, from apex to the base edge

workedExamples.title: Cuboid diagonal angle
workedExamples.prompt: Cuboid 4 × 3 × 12. Find the angle between the space diagonal and the base.

misconceptions.right: Total surface adds the base πr².

misconceptions.wrong: Angle with plane uses the slant edge
misconceptions.right: Use the line and its projection on the plane.

practice.prompt: A(1, −2, 3), B(5, 2, 1). Find AB and the midpoint.
commonErrors: Subtracting a coordinate the wrong way and squaring a sign error (harmless) but averaging wrongly

practice.prompt: A solid is a cylinder (r = 3 cm, h = 10 cm) topped by a hemisphere. Find the total volume and the total exposed surface area.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

given.item: 3D distance and midpoint; volumes of pyramid, cone, sphere; curved area of cone; sphere surface
2D distance/midpoint, cuboid, cylinder, prism areas and volumes

memorise: Pythagoras in 3D; locating the right angle for line-plane angles
formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers. The ISL one-page sheet (Jan 2026) is a third-party summary of the same SL formulas; use the official booklet in the exam. 'Memorise' = needed but not printed.

linkingQuestions.prompt: Which trig ratio do you use once the right-angled triangle is found?

syllabusFlags: Distance/midpoint in 2D are prior learning (unit 1); 3D solids and angles assumed in 'Circular trig' - inferred.
